title: Daisy motif — bobble centre
subtitle: Eight dc petals around a raised bobble-stitch centre, 9 cm
excerpt: A cluster of five bobble stitches replaces the flat chain ring, giving the daisy a raised three-dimensional centre that stands 1 to 2 cm above the petal surface. The bobbles read as pollen heads against the flat petal ring and work best as a single statement motif — a brooch backing, a hat embellishment, or an applique flower on a bag front.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), raised-centre flower motif chapter (Internet Archive). Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870), flower crochet patterns.
heroPrompt: A crochet daisy with a raised bobble-stitch centre in golden yellow, surrounded by eight cream flat petals, on natural linen background in soft daylight. The bobble cluster stands proud of the petal surface, 9 cm across.

chartDefinition.title: Daisy motif — bobble centre
chartDefinition.caption: Centre: five bobble stitches worked into a magic ring, pulled forward on the right side. Petals: eight dc rectangles anchored to the bobble ring base.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five trebles worked into the same stitch with the top loops held on the hook, then drawn together. Pushed to the right side, it forms a rounded raised bump.

content.text: stitches into a tight magic ring, then anchors eight flat petal rectangles around the outside of the ring. The bobbles push to the right side of the work and stand 1 to 2 cm proud of the petal surface. The centre can be worked in a contrasting colour — yellow or orange against cream petals gives the classic daisy read.

A bobble in this context is five trebles worked into the same magic ring, each left with its final two loops on the hook, until the last yarn-over pulls through all six loops together. The more hooks held, the higher the bobble. A four-treble bobble gives a smaller centre; a six-treble gives a higher one.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g of centre colour, 5 g of petal colour — all DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished bobble-centre daisy measures 9 cm across the petals with a 2 cm raised centre in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
bobble (5tr-bo) — five trebles into the same stitch, joined at the top. UK; US uses same name with "dc" for the treble.

Form a magic ring in Colour A. Ch 3 (counts as first tr of first bobble). Work 4 more tr into the ring, leaving the final two loops of each on the hook (5 loops plus the original ch-3 top = 6 loops total). Yarn over, pull through all 6 loops. Ch 1 to close. *Work a 5-tr bobble into the ring the same way. Ch 1 to close.* Repeat from * to * three more times. (5 bobbles total.) Sl st to top of first ch-3. Pull magic ring tail to close. Do not fasten off; join petal colour.

Pick up Colour B at any ch-1 closing chain of the bobble cluster. Work 8 petals as follows: *Ch 10. Turn. Sk first ch, dc across next 8 ch (8 dc). Turn. Ch 1. Dc across 8 sts. Turn. Ch 1. Dc across 8 sts. Sl st into the next ch-1 space of the bobble cluster.* Repeat from * to * seven more times. Fasten off.

definition.title: Daisy motif — bobble centre
definition.caption: Magic ring with five bobble stitches. Eight dc petals on ch-10 foundations anchored around the bobble ring.

content.text: Weave in the Colour A tail through the back of the magic ring. Weave in the Colour B tails through the back of the nearest petal edges. Do not steam-block directly on the bobble cluster — the heat will flatten the three-dimensional structure. Steam from 5 cm above to set the petals only.
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease petals into shape while damp. Reshape the bobble centre gently with your fingers after washing.

The rolled rose (crochet-rose-rolled) extends the three-dimensional principle into a full spiral flower. The puff-stitch centre on the African flower (crochet-african-flower-three-colour) is a flatter cousin of the bobble centre that suits tiled throws.
